doc.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025

title: Getting a Berlin booking agent for a first European tour as leader
summary: Palmer explains his Boston band, new agent Charlotte Jestaedt and the October tour featuring players from The Crossover.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. The current scene that — you’re saying after all these years you finally led a band. Do you have to get an agent to really make that happen for you?

Yeah well you know the — I have a local band, you know a band of cats in Boston that I play with regularly. You know we did a concert last week for International Jazz Day. And so that band, you know we’ve done things, you know, regionally. We played the Chicago Jazz Festival and stuff. But for my latest, my last two or three records I’ve used people in New York and so there are slightly different projects with different kinds of compositions and everything. And so I recently got an agent, a booking agent, that’s based in Berlin. The organization is called Attaché +++. And it’s run by, the director used to work with the agency that booked Kurt Rosenwinkel. And her name is Charlotte Jestaedt, and she started her own company. And so she’s been bringing in people and so when my latest record “The Crossover” came out back in December, we decided to try to throw some dates together to feature the players on that band, on that record, and so Mark Turner is on that record and Marcus Gilmore and Larry Grenadier. And so we’re trying to sell that record, and I’ve got Mark on the tour, he was available to do it, and Jeff Ballard is able to do it, Marcus Gilmore wasn’t able to do it. So in order to like have certain venues have interest, since me myself I haven’t worked a lot as a leader. So I kind of have to have some high-powered people as side people in my project in order to get interest from a lot of venues on the European circuit. So yeah, I don’t think I could have put together the dates that I have — it’s going to be in October — I don’t think I could have done it by myself. I think I would have needed somebody like Charlotte that’s on the inside, that’s already been working with, you know these various venues. But it’s not impossible. I do know people who, you know, put tours together by themselves and you know, they’ll work all the logistics and do all the booking and everything. So you know that kind of thing isn’t impossible you know.
